title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's notes continuing La Longue Marche, with the manuscript paginated around 759 (page 241 of the scan). The previous page computes the 'mixed' fundamental group π_{1,1} = π_1(X_1 minus {a_{1,0}}), with X_1 a torus (the quotient of R^2 by Z^2) punctured at the image of the lattice. It uses Malgoire's description by couples (γ, ℓ) and shows that the commutator xyx^{-1}y^{-1} is the small loop around the puncture. He now opens a section '5) Digression sur les revêtements de germes d'espaces', evidently to give a clean framework for fundamental groups of punctured neighbourhoods: loops 'around the origin', base points or neighbourhoods 'at infinity'.

Definitions on the page:
(i) A germ of space is a pair (S, Φ). S is a topological space and Φ is a filter on S. The improper filter (∅ ∈ Φ, the empty germ) is excluded by a marginal remark. 'Base de filtre' is crossed out in favour of 'filtre'.
(ii) Morphisms (46): Hom((S,Φ),(S',Φ')) is the colimit, over S_i ∈ Φ, of Hom_{Φ_{S_i},Φ'}(S_i, S'). Here Φ_{S_i} is the filter induced on S_i (with the subspace topology). The maps counted are continuous f: S_i → S' with f^{-1}(S'_j) ∈ Φ_{S_i} for all S'_j ∈ Φ', i.e. f maps the trace filter into Φ'. Two such maps define the same morphism if they agree on some smaller member of Φ. Composition is evident.
(iii) Coverings (47): Rev(S,Φ) is the 2-colimit, over S_i ∈ Φ, of the categories Rev(S_i). An object is a covering of some member, and two coverings are identified once they become isomorphic on a smaller member.
(iv) He suggests that 'presumably, at least in good cases', this category is the category of coverings of a suitable topos. The next page confirms this is the projective limit of the small étale topoi of the S_i. He adds that in good cases the category is multigalois or even galois.

The next page continues with connectivity notions. 0-connectedness means the constant functor Ens → Rev is fully faithful; for locally connected S this holds iff every S_i contains a nonempty S_j with π_0(S_j) → π_0(S_i) constant. 1-connectedness means the functor is an equivalence; it adds that every S_i contains some S_j whose components have trivial π_1 → π_1(S_i).

In modern terms this is the fundamental groupoid (Galois category) of the pro-space (S_i)_{i∈Φ}, i.e. the π_1 of the shape of the limit topos. It is the topological analogue of the local fundamental group of a punctured henselian neighbourhood, of fundamental groups at infinity (ends), and of the 'germ' neighbourhoods underlying tangential base points in the Teichmüller/moduli setting of the Longue Marche.
errors: No genuine error. The identification Rev(lim topos) = colim Rev(S_i) is not automatic for arbitrary spaces and arbitrary (non-finite) coverings. It needs finiteness or local-connectedness hypotheses, which Grothendieck explicitly flags with 'sans doute (au moins dans des bons cas)'.

Filter members S_i need not be open; with the subspace topology, Rev(S_i) may behave badly (e.g. not locally connected). The criteria on the next page explicitly assume local connectedness. Restricting to filters with a basis of open sets, or to locally connected members, would be needed in general.

On the next page, the 1-connectedness criterion in terms of π_1(S_{j,α}) → π_1(S_i) being trivial implicitly requires path-connected, semi-locally simply connected members so that coverings are classified by π_1.

ideas.what: Category of germs of topological spaces, defined as pairs (space, filter), with morphisms given as a colimit over filter members of filter-compatible continuous maps
ideas.modern_name: Pro-spaces / germs of spaces along a filter (pro-objects indexed by the filter)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; germs of maps are classical. Pro-objects: Grothendieck (SGA4 Exp. I), Artin–Mazur (1969)
ideas.where_published: Pro-objects in SGA4 I.8 and FGA; this explicit 'germe d'espace' formalism is not known to me in published texts

ideas.what: Coverings of a germ, defined as the 2-colimit of the covering categories of the filter members
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid / Galois category of a pro-space; π_1 at infinity, local fundamental group of a punctured neighbourhood
ideas.usually_credited_to: Local π_1: Grothendieck SGA1/SGA2 (algebraic setting), Mumford, Milnor (links). Ends/π_1 at infinity: Freudenthal, Siebenmann
ideas.where_published: SGA2 (local fundamental group of punctured henselian spectra); SGA1 Exp. V (Galois categories, multigaloisian categories)

ideas.what: Expressing Rev(S,Φ) as coverings of the projective limit of the small étale topoi of the members S_i
ideas.modern_name: Cofiltered limit of topoi and its fundamental group / shape

ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. VI (projective limits of fibred topoi)

ideas.what: Using germs to frame π_1 of punctured neighbourhoods and base points 'around the puncture' in the Teichmüller/moduli Galois program

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a topological 'germ' formalism, including 0- and 1-connectedness of germs, as a foundation for base points and fundamental groups at the boundary in the Longue Marche. He leaves open when Rev(S,Φ) equals the coverings of the limit topos and when it is galois. This framework is essentially what later appeared as tangential base points, but there it was built in an algebraic rather than germ/topos-theoretic way.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mostly historical interest. It documents that Grothendieck intended a uniform germ/limit-topos treatment of 'base points at infinity' for the Teichmüller groupoid, which is close in spirit to later pro-homotopy and shape approaches. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard definitions (germs as pro-spaces, the colimit of covering categories, the limit topos). They are carefully set up but routine for a specialist. The only mild interest is historical: the framework is intended for base points and loops around punctures in the Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: Section title is '5) Digression sur les revêtements de germes d'espaces': 'revêtements de' is an insertion above the line.
The margin note under 'A) Revêtements de germes' reads approximately '(i.e. on écarte le filtre impropre (∅ ∈ Φ) qui correspond au germe d'espace vide)'.

Line after (47): read 'ces revêtements forment une catégorie, sans doute (au moins dans des "bons cas") que nous pourrions être tentés de prendre comme la catégorie des revêtements d'un topos convenable (savoir le topos limite'.
On the next page, 'groupe d'espaces' should read 'germe d'espaces' throughout, and the filter written $\mathfrak{L}$ is Grothendieck's Φ.
Manuscript page number on the page is presumably 759, following 758 and the scan's 240.
